name: Choledochal Cyst

criteria.description: Imaging evidence of cystic dilatation of the bile duct
Presence of abdominal pain, jaundice, and palpable mass (classical triad)
Abnormal liver function tests indicating cholestasis or biliary obstruction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Imaging evidence of bile duct cystic dilatation is mandatory; clinical features and laboratory findings support diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on imaging modalities such as ultrasound, MRCP, or ERCP.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Cystic dilatation of the common bile duct
Classical triad of abdominal pain, jaundice, and palpable right upper quadrant mass
searchTerms: belly pain, yellow skin, and lump
abdominal pain with jaundice and mass
triad of pain, jaundice, and upper belly lump

common.symptomName: Intermittent right upper quadrant abdominal pain
searchTerms: on and off right upper belly pain
intermittent pain in upper right abdomen
jaundice caused by bile duct obstruction
skin and eye yellowing due to blocked bile
pruritus due to liver bile problems

rare.notes: Risk increases with age and cyst type

rare.symptomName: Portal hypertension secondary to biliary cirrhosis
searchTerms: high blood pressure in liver veins

laboratory: Elevated serum bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase
imaging: Ultrasound showing cystic dilatation of bile ducts
Magnetic Resonance Cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) demonstrating cyst morphology
Endoscopic Retrograde Cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) for detailed ductal anatomy
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; considered congenital malformation
other: Histopathology may show bile duct epithelial hyperplasia and inflammation
Todani classification used to subtype cysts

distinguishingFeatures: Progressive obliteration of extrahepatic bile ducts
Typically presents in neonates with persistent jaundice
Absence of cystic dilatation on imaging
Presence of gallstones in the common bile duct
Intermittent biliary colic without cystic dilatation
Imaging shows stones rather than cystic structures

redFlags: Sudden onset of severe abdominal pain with signs of peritonitis (possible cyst rupture)
Persistent jaundice with progressive liver dysfunction
Fever with chills indicating ascending cholangitis
references: Todani T, Watanabe Y, Narusue M, Tabuchi K, Okajima K. Congenital bile duct cysts: classification, operative procedures, and review of thirty-seven cases including cancer arising from choledochal cyst. Am J Surg. 1977 Nov;134(5):263-9.
Loke TK, et al. Choledochal cysts: a review of classification, diagnosis, and management. World J Gastrointest Surg. 2016;8(1):21-30.
